f128.summary: The Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador in Rome, to Charles V (DECODE's '1424' is a typo): the bishop of Veroli's report from Constance on the Swiss diet and cantons arming for France; in cipher, that the Pope's secretary Felice would not show the bishop's own letters, that the report agrees with what the bishop wrote to the postmaster, and that Sessa asked the Pope for a provision for the Swiss business, having opened the peace-and-truce negotiation. Key rebuilt from the sibling letters' contemporary decipherments.
f128.en:
Having written and closed the packet of the duplicate of the 14th of this month, which will come with this, I saw a
letter of the Bishop Verulano, who is at Constance, of which I send a copy herewith. I then sent to His Holiness to beg
him to have me told of any particular, so as to give notice of it where fitting. He sent me Felice, his secretary, who
has told me that the letters he has are from the said Verulano, of the 6th and 7th of this month, where he says that
the diet was over, and that Lucerne did not conclude to give help to the French;

r9873.summary: Sessa to Charles V, a holograph with cipher runs and a postscript wholly in cipher; no decipherment is bound with it (Bergenroth's CSP Spain ii 637 calendars Goicoechea's 19th-century reading, and nos. 636/638 the triplicate and the court abstract, used only as a topic crib). Transcribed in full; each line (a) cipher, (b) reading.
r9873.en:
Where it was needed I have said what Your Majesty commands me about the disbanding of the army in those parts.

[clear text not transcribed]

It was already known through France, though with some additions, because they want to make out that Your Majesty
was holding cortes in Burgos and would then hold them in Aragon and Catalonia, and with the [?grant] that […sig]s
[?it is known] he was coming to [?Italy], which does not please all the ears of this court.

The [?coming] of the Archbishop of Capua will settle these disturbances; it is known today that he left Blois on the
seventh of this month with the articles of truce that he had indicated there, of which His Holiness has ordered a copy
to be given to me.

[?Before] […sas]ission from here, I proposed two things:

r9898.summary: Sessa to Charles V, written on the day of Pavia, before the news: Italy, the Pope and the datary's attempt to bring the Duke over to the French; six runs carry a marginal decipherment of the time, the rest is read here with the key. Not calendared in CSP iii.1.

bne52-7.summary: Sessa reports the Pope's words: Italy confused since the viceroy left; the Pope pressed to join a league that England wants, which he has not and will not consent to; news by way of Bourbon; the French suspicious and fearful; the bishop of Bayeux now an avowed French ambassador; Casale to England; Alberto Pio back from Viterbo; the confirmation of the league; Pescara takes Saluzzo, the army unpaid.
bne52-7.en:
The last letter I wrote to Your Majesty is of the 14th of this month, by a courier who I heard was being dispatched
from Naples, with whom I sent the duplicate of the 12th; and with this goes the duplicate of that one.

As to the troops which ‹rob›…, what the Pope answered me is certain, because someone published it on purpose.

What His Holiness has told me to write to Your Majesty is that everything in Italy is confused and everyone in the
greatest suspicion, which has arisen from the departure of the viceroy without leaving matters here settled; and that
His Holiness has been, and always is, much required and pressed by many to make a league, and in England they desire
it and are dying for new negotiations;

R9874.summary: The last leaf of the letter of 14 April 1524 (R9873): the cipher postscript. Lombardy, the archbishop of Capua, help and money.

R9875.summary: Much of its text recurs in the letter of 14 April 1524 (R9873), so it is probably the duplicate of that letter. Peace and truce, the King of France, England, Lombardy, the viceroy's need, Micer Agostino Foglietta, Alberto Pio da Carpi and the datary.

R9876.summary: A copy of part of the letter of 14 April 1524. The Pope will not declare himself in a league, defensive or offensive. Sessa holds it for certain that, under pressure, the Pope would lean to the French out of fear. Little help, the affairs of Lombardy, and what the archbishop of Capua will bring.

R9879.summary: The same cipher passage as R9881. The archbishop of Capua left France not content. In none of the talks, above all those of peace or truce, did things go well. Madame the Regent sent a person after him to assure him. The Pope by no means wants to show displeasure towards the French. Nothing more is known from England or elsewhere.

R9880.summary: The same cipher passage as R9881 (see there).

R9881.summary: Close to the clerk's decipherment of the time. Sessa has understood that the archbishop of Capua did not leave France content, nor with any of the talks, above all that of peace or truce. Madame the Regent sent a person after him to assure him, so that he would go on with the enterprise; of the one and the other nothing is said. The Pope by no means wants to show displeasure with the French. Of England and of other parts nothing more is known than what Sessa has written.

R9883.summary: Most of its rows are masked or do not read. The war will fall on the Pope's shoulders; the French show more contentment; the Cardinal of England, the archbishop of Capua, the Swiss.

R9884.summary: Close to the clerk's decipherment of the time. All the war will fall on the Pope's shoulders. Neither the Pope nor the Florentines have made more provision of money than Sessa has written. The Cardinal of England and the Regent.

R9885.summary: Too little cipher (8 units) to say.

R9886.summary: Too little is decoded to say. Single words only (work, nobody).

R9887.summary: The Pope; it is impossible to secure; the enemy; Siena; someone in France was not very content; matters of Your Majesty. Several code values here are doubtful.

R9889.summary: The duplicate of R9890's cipher in part. The Pope shows; the due fulfilment; friendship; the Pope has given no more money; the French.

R9890.summary: Its rows read poorly. The Pope; the viceroy; help; the same phrases on friendship and money as R9889.

R9891.summary: The nuncio; the archbishop of Capua; a suspicion; help to someone in France; no money given; the datary; Alberto Pio da Carpi; the viceroy; the war.

R9892.summary: A copy of the cipher of R9893 (24 July 1524): see there.

R9893.summary: Close to the clerk's decipherment of the time. While he waits for Monsieur de la Roxa (as the clerk spells him), the Pope will not talk of anything that touches the state. There is no mention of peace, truce or war, as if he were not Pope. He will not show himself for one side or the other, so everything is in suspense. Sessa does not know what the Pope will do when that man comes, whom he awaits with desire.

R9894.summary: Help; the enterprise of France; time; what would be necessary.

R9895.summary: Sessa has spoken to the Pope; the enterprise; money; the war; what is necessary.

R9896.summary: The datary and the Pope; the Pope 'is here with the King of France'; people very warm with the datary; the nature of his master; Alberto Pio da Carpi; no provision from the viceroy; the need. Madame was content that the second son of the King of France should have an investiture. The suspicion that was taken; this article; after his letter came, no provision has been made.

R9897.summary: The said letter; no time has been lost; Parma; Your Majesty was content; at length; any preparation.

R9899.summary: Too little is decoded to say. Time, place.

R9900.summary: Lombardy and the need; the viceroy; the datary; matters of state; it would be time to come; from England nothing; to enter France; the French would not be acceptable; room given to the enemy; the defence; money; Siena, where the viceroy is.

R9901.summary: Too little cipher (41 units) to say.

R9903.summary: The Pope awaits someone's coming; he is very content that nothing has been done in Lombardy; the viceroy's coming is awaited each day; of England no memory; the league; the defence.

R9904.summary: It shares passages with R9905. The mother of the King of France sends an ambassador; the King of England; the Pope; whether they will come; resistance.

R9905.summary: It shares passages with R9904. The mother of the King of France sends an ambassador; the archbishop of Capua; the viceroy; money; resistance with the greater part.

system: Mixed nomenclator: three-letter code groups for words, names and syllables plus single letters and signs for spelling, with a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
